From Request to Custom Model: How Your Individual AI Model Comes to Life at Virtual Marketer

20 October 2026 · Virtual Marketer Team

The question almost every prospect asks

You've thought through the idea of deploying your own Custom AI model. And then comes the obvious question: what actually happens after clicking "Request"? Who gets in touch, how long does onboarding take, and what is expected of me? An individual AI model is not a software license you activate instantly – it's a joint process centered on your company and use case. The following steps are a representative, generalized sequence – every project is adapted to the respective starting situation.

What distinguishes a Custom model from a generic LLM

A generic language model doesn't know your brand, products, or processes – everything has to be supplied again in the prompt every time. An individual model at Virtual Marketer differs in two respects:

  • Anchored brand knowledge: through fine-tuning on your own approved content, the model learns tonality and structure instead of being re-briefed each time.
  • Factual grounding in your data (RAG): through retrieval-augmented generation, the model draws on current product data or documentation as needed, reducing hallucinations.

The result: fewer manual corrections, less time reformulating instructions, and higher likelihood a text fits on the first try.

How a typical project unfolds: seven steps

1. Initial conversation

A no-obligation conversation about your business goals, not technology: what should the model achieve, who are its users, what does the current process look like?

2. Data and brand assessment

We look together at existing product texts, style guides, and structured data to see how consistent existing content is and where gaps exist.

3. Model scoping

Based on goals and data, we set a realistic framework – better a narrowly defined first use case that works reliably than an overly broad promise the data can't support.

4. Pilot phase

We start with a narrowly limited scope – one product category or a single text format – to train and review the model before larger resources are invested.

5. Review and iteration

Pilot results are evaluated together: does the model hit the desired tone, are formats correct? This step repeats until results meet expectations.

6. Full rollout with monitoring

The model expands to the full planned scope, integrated via API into your CMS or e-commerce platform, with ongoing monitoring.

7. Ongoing optimization

New products or changed guidelines can be incorporated in further training cycles – existing training generally extends rather than being rebuilt.

What you as a customer should contribute

  • Examples of existing content reflecting the desired style
  • Access to product or company data the model should draw on
  • Brand guidelines on tonality, word choice, and format
  • A fixed point of contact for feedback during the project

How long does this actually take?

Duration depends heavily on scope and data situation. As a rough guide: several weeks typically pass from first request to a ready pilot model, with full rollout taking longer depending on project size. What matters more than a fixed deadline is that every phase – especially the pilot and review round – is carried out carefully.

A typical example from practice

A supplier of technical components wanted automated product descriptions in the company's own tone. The initial conversation revealed inconsistent tonality across years of existing texts, so a smaller but consistent set of reference texts was compiled. The pilot combined a fine-tuned model for tonality with a RAG connection to the product feed for accurate specifications. After two review rounds, the model was expanded to the entire catalog and integrated via API, then monitored and readjusted for new product lines.

Frequently asked questions

Do I already need to know exactly what I want to use the model for?

No – a rough idea is helpful; the exact design is developed together during scoping.

What if my data isn't perfectly prepared?

That's the normal case. Clarifying what's usable and where more work is needed is part of the assessment.

Am I contractually bound immediately after the request?

No – the initial conversation first serves to get to know each other before concrete planning follows.

Can I start small and expand later?

Yes, that's the usual path via the pilot phase.

What happens if the pilot results are not convincing?

We look together at the cause – data representativeness, use-case scope – before further iteration, rather than proceeding to full rollout.

The next step is up to you

An individual AI model is created through a structured, joint process – from the first request through a pilot phase to a full, monitored rollout. If you'd like a no-obligation first impression, we invite you to a demo, or request your individual AI model directly.
